findings.title: SC5 round-trip has a test task but no implementing task
findings.description: Success criterion 5 requires `config_to_yaml` to emit `policy` as a plain string. Task 1.4 adds `test_bounds_policy_yaml_round_trip`, but no task touches `config_to_yaml`: Task 1.1–1.3 scope `config.py` work to the enum, the field, and `_validate_world_bounds` only, and the plan repeats the slice design's claim that "`StrEnum` subclasses `str` so `yaml.dump` will serialize it as a plain string automatically." That claim does not hold — `config_to_yaml` goes through `dataclasses.asdict` plus `_serialize_for_yaml`, a dedicated StrEnum→`obj.value` recursion that no task file in the project instructs anyone to write (grep for `_serialize_for_yaml` across `project-documents/` returns nothing). A junior AI following this plan hits a red round-trip test at Task 1.4 with no named step to fix it, at a commit boundary (Task 1.5) that expects green. Add an explicit step in Section 1: extend `config_to_yaml` (or its dict-preparation helper) to convert enum values to strings, and correct the design's serialization assumption.

findings.title: Overweight for a 2/5 slice: duplicated verification and near-identical config tasks
findings.description: 22 tasks across 5 sections for 10 touched files and a slice the design itself rates 2/5. Three steps should be cut or merged: (a) Task 4.1 and Task 4.2 are the same one-line YAML edit plus the same `python -c` load check applied to two files — merge into one task; (b) Task 5.1 re-runs full `pytest` immediately after Task 3.5 already ran and gated on it, with only the manual walkthrough in between — fold 5.1's checkbox into 5.2 step 2, which already says "full test suite passes"; (c) Task 2.3's parametrized `test_all_policies_accept_arrays` asserts only "does not raise", which the per-policy tests already establish, and traces to no success criterion. Everything else in 2.3 (overshoot, negative, multi-width, edge-exact, velocity-unchanged, idempotent flip) maps directly to SC6–SC9 and should stay.

findings.title: `status: complete` while all 22 task checkboxes remain unchecked
findings.description: The frontmatter declares the slice complete and the implementation demonstrably exists in the tree (`src/migratory_server/bounds_enforcement.py`, `BoundsPolicy` and `policy` in `config.py`, `policy: wrap` in both shipped YAML files, `tests/test_bounds_enforcement.py`), yet every step in the file is still `[ ]`. CLAUDE.md's document conventions require checking off each completed item, and an all-open breakdown on a closed slice makes it impossible to tell which of these steps were actually performed versus silently dropped (which matters here — see the required-vs-optional `world_bounds` divergence below). Either check the completed boxes or revert `status` to in-progress.

findings.title: Task 3.1's "required keyword argument" diverged from what shipped
findings.description: Task 3.1 and Tasks 3.4/3.5 plan a required `world_bounds` kwarg, which forces edits at every `SimulationManager(...)` site (22 in `tests/test_simulation.py` alone, plus `tests/test_force_builder.py:201`). The code instead declares `world_bounds: WorldBoundsConfig | None = None` and, when absent, silently falls back to `entity_manager.world_bounds` — an implicit divergence from both this plan and the slice design ("`world_bounds` parameter is added as a required keyword argument"), and a silent fallback value, which CLAUDE.md prohibits. Note it here rather than as a gap: the fallback is defensible for test ergonomics, but the plan and the code should agree, and if the fallback is kept, one success-criteria-adjacent test should pin the fallback's policy resolution.

findings.title: Commit markers are formatted as checkboxes; 4.3 commits ahead of its suite gate
findings.description: Commit placement is otherwise correct — one per working, tested point (1.5 after 1.4, 2.4 after 2.3, 3.6 after 3.5, plus a final docs commit at 5.5), not after every task and not only at the end. Two small deviations: each `**Commit:**` line is wrapped in a `- [ ]` checkbox rather than written as a plain line under its task, and Task 4.3 commits the `policy: wrap` change to `default.yaml`/`test.yaml` gated only on an inline `python -c` load check, with the full suite run deferred to Task 5.1.

findings.title: SC12 (shipped configs opt into `wrap`) is verified only by ad-hoc commands
findings.description: Success criterion 12 asserts the contents of `config/default.yaml` and `config/test.yaml`, and the only checks named are the two inline `python -c` prints in Tasks 4.1/4.2, which a junior AI can satisfy or skip without leaving evidence. The existing `test_default_config_file_loads` (`tests/test_config.py:43-48`) loads `default.yaml` but asserts nothing about policy. One added assertion there (or a small sibling test) would make SC12 machine-gated; the manual walkthrough step 3 already depends on the same fact.

findings.title: All 14 success criteria trace to tasks; sequencing and dependencies are sound
findings.description: SC1→1.1, SC2→1.2, SC3→1.3/1.4, SC4→1.3/1.4, SC5→1.4 (see the implementation gap above), SC6→2.1/2.3, SC7→2.2/2.3, SC8→2.3, SC9→2.2/2.3, SC10→3.2/3.4 (mock patch of `migratory_server.simulation.apply_bounds_policy` — correct target given the `from … import` form), SC11→3.4, SC12→4.1/4.2, SC13→3.5/5.1, SC14→5.2. Section order respects the dependency graph (config field before enforcement module, enforcement module before `step()` wiring, wiring before shipped YAML), with no circular dependencies and no task depending on a later one. Each task carries a concrete, checkable "Success criteria" line. The slice restates no throughput/tick-rate NFR in its success criteria, so no `tests/load/` or CI-gating task is owed here. The design's `SOFT` deferral is correctly kept out of scope (Task 2.1's `match` lists exactly the three variants; the `SOFT` branch now in the code belongs to slice 314).
